KloTouch Editor​

What is kloTouch?

kloBase platform is a modern low-code platform to build enterprise-class cloud-enabled portals and mobile business applications. Its unique layered development empowers to build powerful reusable models for the continuously evolving business needs.

kloTouch is a low-code visual designer tool that helps application development efficiently and effectively.

What is the objective of kloTouch?

kloTouch is a visual designing Page Builder that is effective in building applications that work on portals and mobile applications.

kloTouch has the following objectives:

  • Ease of Operating: It involves least to no complex coding, thus, making it an easy-to-use tool, not only for the modellers but also for common people with limited technical knowledge.

  • Efficient: This Page Builder is programmed in a manner that requires a limited to negligible coding process. This prevents the modellers and developers from losing time by writing lengthy codes, thus saving time.

  • Rich In-Built Features: Multiple add-ons and real-time notifications to name a few, help make it a featureful application.

1.0. Toolbar​

1.1. App Selection​

The App selection drop-down contains a list of apps that have been assigned to the user. By using the drop-down users can select the app on which they are going to work.

​

1.2. Page Selection​

The page selection drop-down is used to select the page. The page dropdown will list all the pages available for the app that have been selected.

Note:This drop-down will be visible only when the app is selected.

1.3. Create page​

The Create Page has three parts:

  • Create Blank Page
  • Create a Page From Wizard
  • Update Page From Wizard
  • Make A Copy of Page

The Create page option is to create a new page for the selected app.

1.4. Undo and Redo​

The undo option is to revert the changes that were made. The use of the redo option is to redo the changes that are undone.

1.5. Painter​

The painter can be used to copy a property or style or vienable of one control to another/multiple controls.

​

Step 1: Select any control/section from the page tree section

Step 2: select the option from the painter

  • Property - all the property details of the selected item will be copied
  • Style - all the styles added to the selected item will be copied
  • Vienable - all the vienable applied to the selected property will be copied

Step 3: Now select the control/section in the page tree to which the copied items should be pasted.

Note: With the painter option, we can apply the copied items to multiple elements, so once the items are pasted, click on `Esc`.

1.7. Save and Edit​

The Save option is used to save the changes that are done.

Note:Save button will be visible only in edit mode.

The Edit option is used to make the kloEditor modifiable.

1.8 Read-Only and Cancel​

The Read-Only and Cancel option is only visible in editable mode.

Clicking read-only mode locks the editor in making further changes.

On click of the cancel icon, any changes made in the editor that are not yet saved will be reverted.

1.9. Validate Page​

This button will validate the page.

Note:It will be visible only in edit mode.

1.10. Section Toggle Buttons​

Section toggle buttons are used to make the sections hide / visible.

Each toggle button is described below:

This is the tree button. This is used to show the hierarchy of the page sectionally. With a click of this button, it will hide the tree section. However, if you click back it will show the tree section again.
This is the preview button. This shows a live view of the changes that have been made to the page. With a click of this button, the preview will disappear. However, on clicking it again the preview section will reappear.
This is the Detail button. The detail section shows the details for the selected item in the tree (page hierarchy). On clicking this button the detail section will disappear. On clicking it again the section will reappear.
Page data model which is equivalent to the UI5 Model in the view. On clicking this button the section will disappear. On clicking it again the page data model section will reappear.
This is the Reset Perspective button. As the name suggests, this is used to resize the section into its original position.

1.11. Delete Page​

To delete the page or screen, a shortcut key will only work, using ALT + BCKSPC .

It will display a confirmation dialog box, confirming to delete the entire page or to cancel the delete as shown below.

2.0. Editor Sections​

Klotouch Editor is divided into four major sections, which are listed below.

  • Tree

  • Preview

  • Detail

  • Page Data Model

2.1. Tree​

The tree section in the kloTouch editor contains the hierarchy of the page.

The tree will contain no data unless a page is created/selected from the toolbar.

Once a page is created/selected it shall automatically reflect in the tree section.

2.1.1 Expand All​

Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (sections, pageLayout, controls, pageArea, actions).

2.1.2. Collapse All​

Collapse All option is to collapse all the expanded sections (sections, pageLayout, wcontrols, pageArea, actions).

2.1.3. Filter​

This filter button will open a popup as :

It will contain fuzzy search, section drop-down and clear filter option.

  • The use of fuzzy search is to filter the items based on the Ids.

  • Section dropdown is used to select and preview a particular section / pageArea of the page. This will filter the tree only for the selected section and its children.

  • Clear filters are used to clear the filters applied.

2.1.4. Cut, Copy and Paste​

Using the cut copy-paste options, we are able to copy paste the controls/section /pageAreas.

**Note:** These buttons are inactive in read-only mode.

2.1.5. Create section​

The create section button is used to create a section and to add required properties from a particular type of transnode.

Clicking on this button, it will open a popup :

In the above popup, we need to mention section id, section title, section type and page data model with which the section is supposed to be binded.

After selecting the page data model, properties list will come in the Page Data Model Node section from where we can select the required properties.

Note: We can edit the section after creation from the Editor.

2.2. Preview​

The Preview section is to preview the page before the final execution.

2.2.1. Preview In​

​

This is also known as the Preview type. The use of preview types is to see the look and feel of the same page on different types of devices. The devices that it can be viewed on are given below. Any new version of the device comes, likewise, it will be updated.

2.2.2. Auto Refresh​

Usage of the auto-refresh button is to refresh the preview in design time i.e. if the auto-refresh is enabled whenever the user changes anything in the page’s metadata it will be previewed (auto-refreshed) automatically.

2.2.3. Preview/ Refresh​

The usage of the preview or refresh button is to refresh the preview page to make the changes visible.

2.2.4. Full preview​

The full preview option is used to view the page in full view.

2.2.5. Full Screen and Close​

The close option is to hide the preview section, to enable the preview section make use of the section toggle buttons

2.2.6. DnD on Preview:​

DnD on Preview is a drag-and-drop feature. It is an option to Drag and Drop properties and elements in multiple ways.

  1. DnD from Unused to MainTree:

Step 1: From the page data model, select the transnode, go to its unused property tab and drag the Property.

Step 2: Drop that Property to any section you want.

After preview, the newly added property will be shown on the screen.

  1. DnD from MainTree to MainTree:

    Users can Drag and Drop any main tree element across the tree.

Step 1: Drag an element from any section and Drop it into the different sections in the same tree.

When an element is dragged and dropped between sections, a prompt appears asking whether to Move or Copy the element. Selecting Move removes the element from the source section and places it in the target section, while selecting Copy duplicates the element in the target section without affecting the source.

Note: The Move and Copy options are shown only when the drag-and-drop action occurs between two different sections.

​

2.3. Detail​

Details of the item selected in the tree section will be shown in this detail section:

This depicts the name or ID of the item selected in the tree.

2.3.1. Properties​

The property tab in the detail section displays the properties that are added and options to add new properties that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, pageLayout, sections, controls).

Refer to this to understand binding concepts.

Value:​

The value field will hold the value provided for the property.

Path:​

In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind.

Parts:​

In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding.

(Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value)

Formatter Functions​

Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field.

Type:​

In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value.

Formatter Options:​

Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI.

Validation Constraint:​

Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values.

Add new Property:​
  • To add a new property, click on the add icon in the property section toolbar.
  • On click of the add icon the properties associated with the control will be listed.
  • Click on the property that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Provide the property value for the newly added property.
​
Property Group:​

The Property group consists of the following:

Property GroupDetails
AppearanceThe appearance property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the appearance of the control. Example: visible, textAlign, wrapping, textDirection.
DataThe data property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the binding values of the control. Example: value, src, text, href.
DimensionDimension property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the dimensions of the control. Example: width, size, height.
BehaviourThe behaviour property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the behaviour of a control. Example: editable, enabled.
MiscProperties other than the above-mentioned groups will come under Misc.
Select All/ None:​

This option is used to select/unselect all the properties.

Cut:​

This option is to cut and paste the property of one control to another control.

Copy and Paste:​

The Copy and Paste options are used to copy/paste one or more properties from one control to another.

Delete Property:​

To delete a property, select the property that needs to be deleted and click on the delete icon in the properties section toolbar.

**![][image13]**

2.3.2. Aggregations​

The Aggregations tab in the detail section displays the aggregations that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls)

Path:​

Binding Path addresses the different properties and lists in a model and defines how a node in the hierarchical data tree can be found.

Examples: $M>/list, $M>/items

Add new Aggregation:​
  • To add a new aggregation click on the add icon in the aggregation section toolbar.
  • On click of the add icon the aggregations associated with the control will be listed.
  • Click on the aggregation that needs to be added, it will be added to the control.
Select All/ None​

This option is being used to select/unselect all the aggregations.

Cut​

This option is to cut and paste the aggregations of one control into another control.

Copy and Paste​

The Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more aggregations from one control to another.

Delete Aggregation:​

For delete, select the aggregation that you want to delete. And click on the delete icon in the aggregation toolbar.

2.3.3. Events​

The Events tab in the detail section displays the events that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls).

Functions​

The controller function name should be given in the field, which will be called in case of the event.

Example of Controller function:

![][image14]
Parameters​

The values passed in the field can be accessible in the function as a parameter.

Add new Event:​
  • To add a new event click on the add icon in the event section toolbar.
  • On click of the add icon the events associated with the control will be listed.
  • Click on the event that needs to be added, it will be added to the control/sections / pageArea.

Note:

  • If we are adding a new event then, it is necessary to add or select the function name.
  • If we are adding a function from the vh as OpenDialog, it will show a popup with all the pageAreas to select,from which we want to navigate.
Select All/ None:​

This option is being used to select/unselect all the events.

Cut:​

This option is to cut and paste the event of one control to another control.

Copy and Paste:​

Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more events from one control to another.

Delete Event:​

To delete an event select the event and click on the delete button from the toolbar.

Events list on page

In the page-level events, we have an option to see the list of events added to this page.

Step 1: Select the page in the Page Builder page tree section

Step 2: Select the events tab in the page detail section

Step 3: enable the toggle button

Once it is enabled, all the events added to this page will be listed below

Navigation Editor:​

NavTo is a kloController API that is used for navigation across the application.

In the Events tab of the Page Builder, if we select NavTo as an event method, the below parameters will reflect for NavTo.

Parameters for Navigation​

The following are the parameters for the navigation:

  • Target Page: It is an F4 of the screens where sections of the current screen, related screen (screens created with related entities) and all the screens of the respected app are present.

  • Section: It is an F4 of all the pagelayouts, pageAreas and sections of the target page.

  • Tags: It shows all the TagIDs maintained in the target screen.

  • Mode: It is a dropdown for different screen modes.

  • App Data: It is a field where the application can send any data while navigating to the target screen.

  • Page Data Model: It is a F4 of all the Data models of the target page.

  • Active Index: It accepts the index to which setActive will be called in the list.

  • Page Data Model Map: It is an array of JSON which expect SourceTransNode & TargetTransnode(i.e SourcetransNode data will be copied to TargetTransnode)

  • Query Parameters: It is for navigation by query(navByQuery).

  • Share Mode: This is for setting whether the mode will be shared after navigating between the source and target pages.

  • Share Model: This is for setting whether the transaction will be shared after navigating between the source and target page.

Specific Style:​
Category:​

In this category field, we can choose the style category that needs to be applied to the selected item.

Style Class:​

Class names should be provided for this field, which will be applied to the selected items. Style class works after selecting the category. In the below image, we have taken the border as our category. Hence, border options are seen in the StyleClass.

Note: The style class should not be empty.

Format Rule:

  1. Always: If the format rule is marked as always, it will always apply the style.
  2. Text Contains: If the format rule is marked as the text contains, it will apply the style if the value contains the one mentioned in the format value.
  3. Formula: If the format rule is marked as formula, it will apply the expression maintained in the format value field and based on the result set of the expression (result is expected to be true or false) the style class will be applied to that control
    1. Example Format value for formula : {= ${$M>/temp/save}?true:false}
Format Value:​

If the format rule is marked with text contain, then text will be taken from this format value field and it will be compared with the control’s value.

If the format rule is marked with a formula, then the expression will be taken from this format value field and based on the result set(the result should be expected to be true or false) of the expression, the style class will be set.

**Example Format value for formula** : {= \${\$M\>/temp/save}?true:false}
Full Row:​

If the full row is marked as true, then the style class will be applied to the entire row, where the control is placed.


Note:

  1. For tree screen type, full-row in style class will be applicable only when the section’s screen type is full row, it will not work for control for control type tree tables.
Add new Style Class:​
  • To add a new style class click on the add icon in the style class section toolbar.
  • On clicking the add icon, a new entry will be created for the style class.
  • Select the category and add the style class accordingly.
Cut, copy, and paste:​

For cut, copy, and paste you need to select the styleclass and then use the cut, copy, and paste accordingly.

Delete​

Select the StyleClass item you want to delete and then click on the delete icon from the toolbar.

Grid Cell Coloring:​

For adding css(background) to whole cell of grid section, user can do following:

  1. Add user defined class in control of grid section

  2. use :has Pseudo-class, and do required styling

    Example: as given below:

    td:has(.invAmountColorWholeCell) {

    background: \#0c8123;

    }

2.3.5(i). Vienable DashBoard:​
​
Control ID:​

The Control ID column displays the available controls on the page.

Entity:​

The transNode of which the control is bound. If it is not marked as true, status and role-based vienable will not work.

Permission:​

The permission of the entity in flavor on which control/element visibility will be decided for logged-in users.

  • If permission is not filled by developer, then proceeds with with vienable calculation
  • If permission is filled by developer, but filled permission not given for logged in user, then the current control/element will be hidden by skipping vienable calculation
  • If permission is filled by developer, filled permission given for logged in user, then proceeds with with vienable calculation
Show As Label:​

If the control is disabled, and the showAsLabel is marked as true then the disabled control will be rendered as a label.

Page Size(S, M, L, XL):​

The page sizes S, M, L, and XL define small, medium, large, and extra-large size page resolutions.

  • If the control is marked as non-visible for page size S, then the control will be hidden for that particular resolution.

  • If the control is marked as disabled for page size S, then the control will be disabled for that particular resolution.

Note: The resolution will be considered based on the parent section’s resolution for control.

page Mode (Create, Edit, Display, Review):​

There are four modes for a page: Create, Edit, Display, and Review. Among the page modes display will be the default mode. We can change the page modes based on the requirements.

​
Role:​

Role-based vienable helps the control to be visible/enabled based on the current logged-in person’s role and object type of the bound entity. For this role-based configuration, KloTuner is used.

For role-based vienable, config has to be maintained for the respective entity.
If it is not maintained in the entity level, It will consider the role maintained in the app-level.

While configuring the config table, provide the s_role_rollup value as below:

Roles_role_up
Owner10
Supervisor20
Reviewer30
Overlooker40
Status Group():​
​

Status: open, approved, accepted, processed, rejected, completed.

Based on the s_status_group, s_status, and object type for that particular entity, we will be able to make the control visible/enabled. For status-based configuration, Klotuner is used.

Note: Similar to role-based vienable, status-based vienable status configs have to be maintained for the entity.

​
Result:​

In the result column, we can see the final result of how the controls will be rendered, for the selected page mode, selected role, and selected status group.

The yellow background in the column header represents the selection of the column.

2.3.5(ii). UI Auth:​
Element Id:​

It is the control ID of the control.

Object Type:​

For this object type, UI Auth will be applied.

Role:​

For this role, the UI Auth will be applied.

Status:​

For this status, UI Auth will be applied.

Mode:​

For this mode, UI Auth will be applied.

Mode Value:​

This will determine the control’s visibility / enableness.

Add new UI Auth:​
  • To add a new UI Auth click on the add icon in the toolbar of the UI Auth section. On click of the add icon, a popup will be displayed.
  • In the popup select the control for which UI Auth needs to be applied.
  • Select the role, mode, object type, and status after selecting press OK. A new entry will be added in the UI Auth section.
Vienable Runtime precedence:​

If all the vienable sections (screen size, screen mode, role, status) are maintained for control, below will be the flow of the section it will take into consideration.

2.3.6. Modeller​

The Modeller tab in the detail section displays the modeller only if the modeller is available for the selected section type.

A modeller is generally used for modelling the sections.

Note: The modeller will load only if the particular section is visible in the preview section. To access the modeller of a section select that particular section in the tree section to preview that particular section.

Card & cardList Modeller:​

WYSWYG (What You See What You Get)

Card WYSWYG allows the users to arrange/resize controls of the Card. The Card WYSWYG is available in the tab called “Modeller” of the kloTouch Editor if the section type is given as cardlist/card.

These are the following steps to use WYSWYG:

Step 1: Select the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”) or any child of the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”).

Step 2: Open the “Modeller” tab. Users can arrange/resize controls as required.

Step 3: For arranging the controls, the user can simply drag a control and drop it anywhere on the axis as per the requirement.

While doing the arrangement or resizing, if any other control exists in the same axis, red lines will be shown.

Step 4: For resizing the controls, Users can simply click on the controls and resize them as they want.

Before resizing:

After resizing:

NOTE: Users can select multiple controls(by holding the control) and “Make the same size” (Vertically/Horizontally).

Reveal Grid: With this button, one can enable and disable the gridlines.

Tabular Card Modeller: On clicking this button, a tabular card modeller will open where the user can manually provide a column/row span for the alignment of the card/cardList.

Alignment: Options for Alignment, space distribution, equal size:

Modeller Size: To make the card modeller screen size the selected item’s size one uses the modeller size (Tab, Desktop, etc) tab.(This option has been disabled: To use this, change the screen resolution from preview type)

Absolute/Relative: The absolute button will make the modeller as the previous version without additional features. On the other hand, the Relative button will set the modeller section as the newer version(5.7) with all the additional features.

The card is generally a css gridlayout and the cardlist is generally a list of css grid layouts.

Screen SizeSpans available
XL, L36 column span
M24 column span
S12 column span

For more information about CSS grid layout click here

Note: if column span and row span are not maintained for a particular screen size then it will pick from the default span (if maintained). But if either of the one is maintained then it will pick both the values from that particular screen size.

Note: As the Page Area of type Dialog doesn’t have any direct assignment with any of the page Layouts, the Modeler/preview will not be available.This Modeling can be achieved by adding that particular section to any other page Area (which is assigned to any page Layout). Once the modelling is completed, reassign to the Dialog Page Area.

Grid Modeller:​

Grid modeller is used to model the grid type section. Using this grid modeller we will be able to change the column width, we can assign filters, and sort for a particular column.

Pivot Modeller:​

There are two types of pivot modellers

  • Design time
  • Run time

Note: The difference between the design time and run time modeller is that the design time modeller cannot be modified by end users it is predefined by the developers.

The design time pivot can be set as the default view of the section by use of the ‘default report’ property of the section.

Design Time Modeller :​

Design time pivot will be created by the developers which will be predefined, and cannot be modified by the end users.

Step 1: Select a section which is of type card list or grid type and then add the report

Step 2: Select the newly created record and click on the modeller to see the design time pivot modeller.

Note: For how to use it you can refer to this document Pivot Modeller

Run Time Modeller:​

The pivot modeller is used to configure the grid and card list subscreen. You can customise the pivots and charts based on your preferences, using this modeller.

These are the following steps to enable the run time Pivot Modeller:

Step 1: Select a section which is a card list or grid type and then add a toolbar to that subscreen.

Step 2: Now in the toolbar detail, add two properties (reportSelectionField and pivotModellerButton) and mark these properties as true.

Once the above properties are added during the design time, the modeller button and view selection will appear in the toolbar of the table during runtime.

Note: For how to use it you can refer to this document Pivot Modeller

CSS Grid:​

CSS grid is the screen container that can hold page areas or sections. Under CSS Grid, users can arrange subscreen controls in any way they want in any layout.

Step 1: Make the Page Layout or Page Area screen type as ‘CSS Grid’.

Step 2: Right-click on that page layout or page area and add the page layout data to it.

After assigning the page section or PageArea, the page layout or page Area will look like this.

Step 3: Now go to Modeller then click on ‘Tabular card Modeller’.

Step 4: Add row/column-span to align subscreens as you want.

Model Path/TransNode:​
PropertiesDescription

Property DescriptionDisplays the property description.

node_typeNode Type determines the type of the model path.

Node Type:​
  1. Entity: Entity defines a single entity (single row in a database table).
  2. Entity Set: An entity set is a set of entities (an entire table in a database).
  3. Query: Query which is associated with the entity.
  4. Other: Other types of transnode represent that the node is not associated with any entity. Its data can be bound from the controller.
onArrive:​

  1. Blank: If the model path is marked as blank then the data will not be set to its folded path.

  2. First: If the model path is marked as first then the first index of its entityset(folded from) will be set.

  3. History: If the model path is marked as history then it records the active index of the entityset.

    For example: if the model path is marked as history, then each selection of entity will be recorded.

  4. None: If the model path is marked as none then the data will not be set for that path.

Set_active_if:​

Set active is classified into three categories as listed below:

  1. Always: Always defines navigation without any pre-conditions except menu navigation.
  2. Saved: Saved means navigation is permitted only if there is no dirty object in the transaction. If dirty entities are found, the Save confirmation dialog comes to ask the user if he/she wants to save the changes, otherwise, navigation is cancelled.
  3. Valid: Valid is a default value. Valid means navigation is permitted if there are no dirty objects or dirty objects are in a valid state with no error. If dirty objects are there and in an error state, the errors are highlighted on the page for the user to correct before moving forward. If the mode path’s set_active_if is provided as “valid”, on time of navigation the onValidate function (if the function is maintained in the <entity_name>.ts file) will be called.

Please refer to the below matrix for all combinations of set_active_if:

alwayssavedvalid
Within ScreenSame index of entityset(tab selection change)CREATENo Validation, No Dirty PopupNo Dirty PopupNo Validation
Not CREATENo Validation, No Dirty PopupDirty PopupValidation
Different index of entitysetAnyNo Validation, No Dirty PopupDirty PopupValidation
Close DetailAnyNo Validation, No Dirty PopupDirty PopupValidation
Different ScreenThrough ManuAnyDirty PopupDirty PopupDirty Popup
Through Link inside screenAnyNo Validation, No Dirty PopupDirty PopupValidation
q_saved_qur_action:​

  1. Execute: Execute will autofire the query while rendering the page. This is set as the default value.

  2. Fill: If the q_saved_qur_action is marked as true then the “q_saved_qur_id” will be filled on search.

  3. None: None means it will take no action.

3.0. Page​

The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

3.1. Page Creation:​

Create Blank Page: Step 1 - Select the Add icon to create a Blank Page To create a new page click on the Add icon from the top toolbar. Three options will be shown, from those options select ‘Create Blank Page’. After selecting the option a popup will be displayed.
Step 2 - Fill the popup to create a new page In the popup, provide the ID and name/title for the new page. After providing the details, click on the Submit button.

Note: Newly created pages will be updated in the database only after saving. To save click on the save icon at the top toolbar (right side of the edit action button).

PropertiesUsage
DescriptionDescription for the page.
leadentityComing Soon
docidThe ID/text will be displayed along with the title (bindable).
iconIf value is provided, the icon will be displayed in front of the title.
navbyqueryIn case user is navigating from a different page to the current page with passing the QP (Query Parameters) in navTo, then this field is mandatory to filter the data based on the query properties passed Example: {“sourcePath”: “search”}
navbykeyIn case user is navigating from a different page to the current page with passing the D (entity unique key) in navTo, then this field is mandatory to set that particular entity’s index as active. Example: {“sourcePath”: “list”}
Pip enabledIf marked as true, picture-in-picture(PIP) mode will be enabled for the page.
screencontainerdefaultDefault page Layout ID for the page can be provided here.

screencontainertabPage Layout ID for the tab can be provided here

​
Create Page from Wizard:​
Step 1 - Select App and click on the Edit button Step 2 - Page selection Click on the add icon dropdown and select “Create a page from wizard”.
Step 2 - Provide page information Once the wizard popup is displayed, provide the screen information. Select the Data Source and check whether Page ID, Page Title, Menu Text, Icon, or Menu Group is pre filled or not. Page Id, Page Title & Manu Text should be prefilled and will be Entity`s description or entity`s ID. Select the Data source (entity or query) by clicking on the vh icon, and give page ID and Page title and Menu Information. By default, the entity id will be Page Title. Page Id should be unique in the particular app, if we are creating more than one pages with the same entity, the Page Id will be auto incremented by 01 as a suffix. Menu Group will come from the app header. We can provide a menu text and can select a group and icon to be displayed there from the Choose button . It will update the page to the selected menu group. Menu Icon will come from Entity’s icon or default icon will come. Also we can allow operations by clicking on the icons provided: This shows the options to perform CRUD in the main entity. These icons are for Add, Edit, Delete, Multi Delete, Download Excel operations respectively. By default all these icons are selected. We can deselect them by simply clicking on the icons. Click on Next.
Step 3 - Select the required section, relation, type, template, position and actions. The screen is displaying different requirements to select for all section types of each relation. Relation: It shows the return entity name along with the relationId of the entity. Section: It shows the type of section of the corresponding relations. Type: It shows the screentype of the section that will be created using the relationid. Display options: It shows the different templates of the screentype. It depends on the Type selected for the section. Position: It shows the position of the sections in the application. Eg: If a relation has the Position as dialog, then it will appear as a dialog whenever navigation happens to the section. Required Actions: It shows the option to perform CRUD in the corresponding section created from the relation. We can select the relation required from the checkboxes displayed on the left most of the screen. NOTE: A 1:1 relation can be added only as a Detail section and is supported with Form and Card screen types. The section can be placed as a Section or Subsection on the page.Template Id is supported as Read Only and Inline Editable Section type can be selected from the drop down for different sections (search, list and detail). For List type of section, we can edit the template from the dropdown (Read Only, Inline Edit or Popup Edit) We can specify the position for sections as section(tab) or subscreen or dialog. Actions can be provided to each section type by selecting the icons from required actions.(These are selected by default). The relations have a DND (Drag-and-drop) feature, if we are changing the sequence then the sections will also be generated accordingly. Template tab will not be there for wizard dialog. The detail screen for all child entities will be opened in a popup. Template types: Read Only It is non-editable. We will get an edit button for the detail tab only, not for relation list tabs. Inline Edit We will get the Edit button for the selected tab in the relation list. Popup Edit We will get an edit button in each row of data. Click on Next at the bottom of the screen.
Step 4 - Specify the availability of fields on screen On navigating to the screen. all the properties of the lead entity & the selected relations will appear. All the properties will be selected for the detail section(if Detail is selected) & first 5 properties excluding the primary keys will be selected for the list(if List is selected). Select the required properties for the transnodes. Here, availability of fields can be specified on screen by clicking on the respective checkboxes for different sections (Search, List and Detail). On selecting the navigation icon, it will create a link for the property or field in the list to navigate to the detail section. (Only one can be selected.) DND (Drag and Drop) features are available for the fields. The sequence will be arranged accordingly on the screen. If we are selecting any property in the search, it will be automatically selected in list and detail. If we are selecting any property in the list, it will be automatically selected in detail. At least one primary key must be selected. (Selected by default) Primary key selection is not mandatory in the search section. NOTE: In the image, we have selected properties for d_no_header. In the same way you can select related entities (d_no_users, d_no_tasks, d_no_item) properties. To select properties for related entities, click on that entity and select its properties. The buttons are to go back to the previous screen, save as draft, save, and for discarding the page created respectively. On click of the save button, the page will be created and saved. On click of the Preview button, the page will be created but will not be saved. On Click of the Discard button the page will not be created and dialog will be closed Now after specifying all required fields, click on Save button. This will create and save a new page.
Note: For list nodes, at least one primary key needs to be selected.
After clicking on save, the page created from wizard will look similar to the image below. NOTE: Now we can do necessary changes from the Editor or can update the page from wizard also. The relation section name is taken from relation id ,hence the relation sections are created with similar name incremented by 01 as suffix Refer to this document for the tree hierarchy In desktop view, the list screen will look like this as shown below: After navigating to detail: Screens will be created for mobile view also. It's PageArea screentype will be Tiles and section screenType will be card in mobile view: Button Configurations in screen: Buttons will be added separately for separate tabs and it will be based on the display options. Buttons will appear at the top right corner. Save and Cancel buttons will be visible only in edit mode. If we want to switch between tabs without saving, it will show a popup. Either edit or save button will be shown always. Scroll will start after the edit and save buttons. On selecting the multi delete button while page creation, it will allow you to select multiple items and delete at a time in the grid. If the multi select delete button is not selected, then the delete button will not be visible on the list type of section. Grid behaviour in the Relation Transnode On click of the link in the relation list, it opens up the Popup in the same mode as that of the screen mode. On click of the PopupEdit button of the grid of type Popup Edit grid, opens up the popup in the edit mode if the current screen mode is not in either create mode or edit mode.The next and previous buttons can be used to see the next and previous items details. With the click of the OK button, data modified will be saved and the popup will be closed. On click of the Cancel button, the refreshTransnode api will be called which will call refreshP BOL API on the transnode data. (i.e., Changes will be reverted ) and the popup will be closed. On click of the Add button in the toolbar, the popup opens in the Create mode. With a click of the OK button, data will not be saved, as the previous mode is in create mode. On click of the Cancel button, the refrestTransnode api is called the refreshP BOL API on the transnode data and the popup will be closed. Change in Page Data model Structure Now in the Page Data Model, there is no option to move entity properties from unused to used and transnodes will come in the hierarchy of the respective folded path. Note: If a parent transnode is getting deleted, then its respective child will be deleted as well. Tags During wizard page creation, a default tag will be created to navigate to the detail page, this default tag can be used for deep link navigation. Update Page from Wizard: Developers can modify the screen created from Wizard using the Update Page From Wizard option. All the elements selected during the creation of the screen will be auto-selected in the Update Page From Wizard. Example: Sequencing, adding, delete of properties/sections/layouts can be done using Update Page From Wizard. It will reopen the wizard popup with all provided screen information. Cardinality update when screen is created from wizard If we are creating a page from wizard and it has relations with any particular cardinality. After page creation, if we are changing its cardinality from Data Studio,it will not be reflected on the UI automatically. We have to delete the transnodes manually and have to create them again. For Example: If the user is creating a wizard with 1:n relation and after creation, the cardinality of the relation will be changed to 1::1 from the Data Studio and tries to update the page from wizard, before that the user have to delete the transnodes manually and have to recreate it again.
Deletion of a section or control​

If we are deleting a section from Page Builder, it will be updated on wizard also:

  • In the same way it will work for other sections.
  • If we delete any property from the Page Builder, it will be deselected from the wizard popup also.
  • Anything we are changing from Page Builder, it will be reflected in the wizard popup.
  • In the screen we are deleting data from the parent entity, then it will delete all the entries from the child entity also.
Make a copy of the page:​

Step 1: Click on ‘Make a Copy of Page’

Step 2: After clicking on ‘Make a copy of page’ the below screen appears with all the details filled already. If you want then you can modify the detail as well.

Step 3: Click on the submit button and the current page will be copied to the provided app.

Note: The above example was making a copy of a particular page in the same app.

What if we are copying a page in a different app and that app doesn’t have the associated entity?

If we are doing so then the Page Builder sends an alert message (“Entities/Queries are not found in the app. Do you still want to continue?”)

Note: If we click on OK then the particular screen will get copied in the target app without a pagedata model. And if the target app contains the associated entity then the screen will render with all data.

4.0. Page Layout:​

PageLayout is the topmost layer embedded with the page. At runtime, only one pageLayout will be picked based on the device type. The detail of which pageLayout needs to be picked is maintained in the page’s properties (screencontainerdefault, screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screenontainertab). If the property for a specific device type is not maintained then the default pageLayout will be rendered.

Example: If the page is being loaded on the desktop, and the screencontainerdesktop property is not maintained (empty) then the pageLayout ID maintained in the screencontainerdefault property will be rendered.

  • Layouting can be also possible using a pageLayout.
  • Supporting layouts are
    • Grid Layout
    • Default
    • Dialog
    • Fit To Area
    • Flexible Column (Deprecated, Use Two Column Pagelayout Instead)
    • Horizontal Splitter
    • Object Page
    • Stack
    • Sticky
    • Tab
    • Tiles
    • Vertical Splitter.
    • Two Column
  • Layout will be maintained in the screetype property of the Page Layout.

Step 2: A newly created pagelayout will be added.

Note : We can rename it by a right click on the newly created layout and select the option Rename (ensure that the new Id given should be unique among other layout Ids).

5.0. Page Area​

The Page area is the next level in the page hierarchy after the Page Layout. Page areas are embedded with the pagelayout. The detail of the page Area that needs to be rendered for the page area will be maintained in the Page Layout’s Layout Data section.

As the page area also has layouting types, supported layouting types are object page Layout, tab, goto, stack, grid layout, and splitter layout. Layout type will be maintained in the screetype property of the Page Layout.

6.0. Sections​

Sections are the building blocks of the pages. The page can have multiple sections, and the sections are embedded in a page Area. The detail of which section should be rendered for a page Area will be maintained in the page Area’s Layout data section.

A popup will appear. Select our newly created section from the popup as shown: Section layout will be added to your page area.

Tree​

The Tree Screen Type is designed to represent hierarchical data in a structured manner. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organisational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets.

Implementation:

Data Preparation:​

To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure. Here’s a sample JSON array:
[{
"key_01": "value_1",
"key_02": "value_2",
"key_03": "value_3",
"child": [{
"key_01": "value_11",
"key_02": "value_22",
"key_03": "value_33",
"child": [{
"key_01": "value_111",
"key_02": "value_222",
"key_03": "value_333",
"child": [{
"key_01": "value_1111",
"key_02": "value_2222",
"key_03": "value_3333",
}]
}]
}]
}]

JSON Structure

  • Each object represents a node in the tree.

  • The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes.

  • Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship.

We will store the data in other type transnode.

Screen:​

Step 1:

Create one pageArea with screentype, fit_to_area and a section with screentype, tree.

In the section layout, add one property autoHeight as true. This ensures that the section dynamically adjusts its height based on the content displayed.

Step 2: Create an other type transnode.

Step 3: Add Controls for Data Binding

  • Create controls within the section for each key in your JSON data (key_01, key_02, key_03).

  • Bind the section to the other type transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data.

  • Ensure that each control is correctly bound to the corresponding key in the JSON structure.

8.0. Aggregation​

An aggregation is a way for one control (called a parent) to reference another subordinate control (called a child).

9.0. Embedded section​

By using this embedded section we can embed sections or containers from other pages to our current page.

Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Also, the title, icon and actions provided for the embedded subscreen will not be rendered. Page layout type” flexible_col” is not supported inside embedded section.

9.1. Embedded section Creation:​

To create an embedded page create a page Layout in the page where the section is embedded from. In our current page create an embedded section.

In the layout data of the embedded section provide the value below:

  • flavor.pageId.pageContainerId if it's a separate app.

  • pageId.pageContainerId if the embedding page is from the same app.

Note: Developers can pass supported navTo() properties from a parent screen to an embedded child screen. TN and NT parameters will be passed to child functions (such as onPageEnter() and onSectionEnter()) only when they are explicitly maintained in the embedded section's screenParameters configuration.

9.2. Embedded Config​

The properties available in the embedded config are listed below. Embedded config can be added from context menu of the embedded section

​

NAMETYPEDEFAULT VALUEDESCRIPTION
flavorstring-App from which the page should be picked from. App is mandatory only if the app of the screen to be embedded and the app of the hosting page are different.
screenidstring-ID of the screen. Mandatory
subscreenidstring-ID of the subscreen. Mandatory.
isTransactionSharedbooleanfalseIf true, the hosting screen and the embedded screen will share the transaction. Else, transaction will be different for both the screens
isSharemodebooleanfalseIf true, the hosting screen and embedded screen will share the mode. When mode is set via the controller for the hosting screen, the same screen will be set to the embedded screen as well and vice-versa. Else, the mode will not be shared. When set to the hosting screen, the mode will not be set to the embedded screen.
tnmapArray<JSON>-An array of JSON with the keys fromtn and totn. The value of the keys should be the transnode relation ID of the host screen and embedded screen respectively. The transnode of the embedded screen will be added as a child to the transnode of the hosting screen so that when setActive is called on the parent transnode, data will be set on child. Example : [{"fromtn": "no_hdr_list", "totn": "detail_embedded"}]
screenParametersINavToDataThis property expects a JSON the same as the navTo parameters. All the navTo parameters can be passed here. Flavor, Screen ID, subscreen ID, isTransactionShared, isSharemode and tnmap can also be passed as key-value pair here instead of separate properties.

12.0. Layouting​

12.1. Flexible_col (Deprecated, Use Two Column Pagelayout Instead):​

All the page Area ID(s) provided in the page’s layout section will implement the master-detail-detail paradigm by displaying up to three pages (page Areas) in separate columns. For a Flexible column layout, only three columns will be rendered, if more than three layout containers are provided in the layout section it will take the first three layout containers/sections.

Configuration:​
  • For using the flexible column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as flexi_column.
  • In the layout section of that pageLayout add the layouts.
  • The setLayout() method was used in Flexible Column to define the layout width. As Flexible Column is now deprecated, it is recommended to use setFirstColumnWidth() in pagelayout type Two Column to configure column widths.

Example:

Flexible_col one Column Expanded

Flexible_col two Column Expanded

Flexible_col three Column Expanded

12.2 Two Column​

It is similar to a flexible column. The only difference is that it can only implement the master-detail paradigm up to two pages only. And also unlike a flexible column it provides a horizontal splitter between the two pages..

Configuration:​

  • For using the two column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as two_column.

  • Assign pages and sections.

  • Use setFirstColumnWidth() to configure column widths.

two_column one Column Expanded

two_column two Column Expanded

12.3. Stack​

Stack is a layout structure where the required elements show up one by one on a particular action based on the given metadata.

Configuration:​
  • For using the stack layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as stack.

Example:

We have a pageLayout of screentype stack:

Stack will render only one layoutSubscreen at a time. As a default, the first layoutSubscreen is rendered.

When it is navigated to the second layoutsubscreen it hides the first one & displays the pageArea it is navigated to.

12.4. Tab​

Tab Layout represents a collection of tabs with associated content. The number of tabs rendered will be equal to the number of section/section container ID(s) given in the layout Data section. The tab title will be taken from the section/page Area’s title property, the tab title will only be visible if the flags are maintained in the layout data section and the showTitle property is marked as true.

Configuration:​

  • For using the tab layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as tab.

  • In the detail section, mark the showTitle as true.

  • After adding the showTitle as true, in the layout section. For the layouts added (pageArea / section ) add the property showTitle and title, provide the values.

Note: selectedKey reflects the currently active tab/section — it is not a one-time "default tab" setting. If bound to a data field, the Tab control will always show whichever tab that field currently holds, and will keep showing it on subsequent loads/refreshes unless the field's value is explicitly reset. If the supplied key doesn't match any tab/section currently rendered, the control falls back to another available tab instead of forcing the configured one. To always land users on the same section regardless of prior state, drive it explicitly through navigation rather than relying on selectedKey alone.

Now similar to the object page, it is possible in the tab also to create a header for title content and sections, subsections for block contents.

  • Add the type of PageAreas / sections as header, section or subsection.

14.0. Controller​

14.1. Hook Methods:​

onPageInit​

onPageInit hook method will be called only once as soon as the controller is loaded

The transaction, model , and the UI is yet to be created for this, so those will not be available in this method.

onPageModelReady​

onPageModelReady event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the data is not set to the model yet.

From this hook method developer can call skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then developer should be responsible for setting the data is the model

onPageEnter​

onPageEnter hook method will be called whenever the page enters the visible area by means of navigation(both forward and backward navigation).

If the navigation is within the same page, this method will not be triggered

onPageExit:​

onPageExit hook method will be called in the source page whenever the user navigates to a different page

onPageDestroy:

onPageDestroy hook method will be called only once when the page is destroyed.

Page will be destroyed during the back navigation

Example : if you are navigating back from PageB to pageA then PageB will be destroyed

15.0. Entity File​

15.1. Hook Methods:​

onValidate:​

If the transNode’s onarrive (in the transNode’s detail section) is provided as valid then, onValidate will be called during navigation.

onAfterCreate:​

onAfterCreate method will be called once the new entity is created.

onDelete:​

The onDelete method will be called once the entity is deleted.

15.2. Setter & Getter:​

Setter function will be called once the entity property value is changed.

Example:

public set  firstName(new\_value:string){

    if(new\_value \== this.firstName) return;

    this.name:string \= new\_value\+" "\+this.lastName;

    this.s("firstName",new\_value,"string",false,false);

}

Getter function will be called whenever the entity property is getting read.

Example:

public get name():string{

    return this.Firstname \+" "\+this.lastName

}

16.0. Where used list​

The Where Used list can be accessed from the context menu of the following elements:

  • Page
  • Page Area
  • Section
  • Transnode

To open the Where Used dialog:

  1. Right-click on the required element (Page, Page Area, Section, or Transnode).
  2. The context menu is displayed.
  3. Select Show Where Used from the menu.
  4. The Where Used dialog opens, displaying all references for the selected element.
​

When clicking on Show Where Used from the context menu, a Where Used dialog box opens. This dialog displays all references to the selected item within the current application.

Dialog Layout​

The Where Used dialog is divided into two sections:

  • Left Panel (Tree View)
    Displays a hierarchical list of all references for the selected item.
  • Right Panel (Details View)
    Shows detailed information for the reference selected in the left panel.

Selecting an entry in the tree view updates the details shown in the right panel.

Supported Elements​

The Where Used feature is available for the following elements:

  • Pages
  • Page Areas
  • Sections
  • Transnodes
Reference Checks by Element Type​

  • Pages
    The system checks for references in:

    • Application menus
    • Home pages
    • Other pages (including embedded sections and tags)
    • Associated files (controllers, utils)
    • Navigation events within the current page (for example, navTo events)

  • Page Areas
    The system checks for references in:

    • Associated files(controllers, utils)
    • NavTo Events, layouts in other pages and the current page

  • Transnodes
    The system checks for references in:

    • Binded data paths
    • Associated files(controllers, utils)

Navigating to Referenced Objects​

The Where Used dialog allows direct navigation to referenced application objects.

In the left tree section, a Navigate button is displayed for application-level objects. When you click this button:

  • A new tab opens automatically.
  • The relevant tool or editor is loaded.
  • The referenced object is preselected and highlighted in the opened tool.

Automatic Alignment Handling for Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid Sections​

For Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. So the column header and the control will be aligned as per the standards based on the domain and control type

Numeric Field Alignment​

If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is Integer or Decimal, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value Right.

This automatic alignment is applied only when:

  • The control is an input-based control.
  • The control is bound to a property of domain type Integer or Decimal.
Alignment Updates on Control Changes​

During updates, if:

  • A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or
  • A new binding is added to the control,

the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly.

​

Domain/data typeData alignmentHeader Alignment
Boolean [if control is checkbox or switch]CenterCenter
BlobN/AN/A
StringLeftLeft
ClobLeftLeft
DateLeftLeft
DecimalRightRight
Integer(16)RightRight
Integer(32)RightRight
Integer(64)RightRight
Integer(8)RightRight
TimestampLeftLeft

Control-Specific Alignment Rules​

The following alignment rules are applied automatically:

Control TypehAlign Value
Switch, Check BoxCenter
Button, KloActionRight
​
Auto Grid Behavior​

For Auto Grid sections, automatic alignment is applied only in the Desktop view.

For the Mobile view, the default alignment behavior is retained and no automatic alignment adjustments are applied.
